suggestions.assertion: Adapter task has adapter_id in incoming variables
suggestions.reason: This only checks presence, not correctness. It would pass even if adapter_id were an arbitrary string (e.g. "foo") rather than a real instance id from adapters.json. In this run the value happened to be correct ("ServiceNow", verified against platform/adapters.json), but the assertion itself doesn't discriminate a wrong instance id from a right one. Consider requiring the value to match an actual adapters.json instance id, or match the real asset's pattern of a $var.job reference.

suggestions.assertion: merge has at least 2 items in data_to_merge
suggestions.reason: Checks count only, not that the items actually correspond to the job variables named in the task (deviceName, vlanId). A merge with 2 arbitrary/irrelevant fields would also pass this assertion. Consider asserting the specific variable names appear in data_to_merge.

No assertion checks that the workflow graph is fully connected from workflow_start to workflow_end with no orphaned/unreachable tasks, or that inputSchema declares the job variables referenced by the merge task (deviceName as string, vlanId as integer). Both were correct in this run and would be a meaningful outcome to check, since a workflow with a dangling task or a schema mismatch would otherwise slip through undetected.

eval_feedback.overall: The expectation set is solid and reasonably discriminating for the core merge->adapter wiring pattern (the 'variable' vs 'value' and app/locationType-source checks are good, hard-to-fake assertions). The main gap is that a couple of presence-only checks (adapter_id present, >=2 merge items) would pass for incorrect values/content, not just correct ones.

expectations.evidence: outputs/create-change-request-workflow.json task a1a1.variables.incoming.data_to_merge: [{"key":"deviceName","value":{"task":"job","variable":"deviceName"}},{"key":"vlanId","value":{"task":"job","variable":"vlanId"}}]. The job-variable reference objects use the key "variable" (not "value") exactly as in the real production asset helpers/assets/vendor-servicenow.json task 'aab9' (merge, Create Change Request workflow): {"key":"title","value":{"task":"job","variable":"title","editable":true}}. Verified by directly reading that asset file with jq.

expectations.text: Adapter task body wired via $var to merge output, not inline $var inside object
expectations.evidence: task b2b2 (createChangeRequest).variables.incoming.body = "$var.a1a1.merged_object" — a single top-level string reference to the merge task's output, not a literal object containing embedded $var strings. Matches the real asset workflow's cc49.body = "$var.aab9.merged_object" pattern exactly.

expectations.text: Adapter task has adapter_id in incoming variables
expectations.evidence: task b2b2.variables.incoming.adapter_id = "ServiceNow", present alongside body. Cross-checked against platform/adapters.json which lists {"id":"ServiceNow","package_id":"@itentialopensource/adapter-servicenow",...} confirming "ServiceNow" is a genuine adapter instance id, not a fabricated value.

transitions.b2b2 = {"workflow_end":{...,"state":"success"},"c3d4":{...,"state":"error"}} — b2b2 (createChangeRequest) has an explicit error transition routed to intermediate task c3d4, avoiding the duplicate workflow_end key problem while still ultimately reaching workflow_end.

Task keys in outputs/create-change-request-workflow.json: workflow_start, a1a1, b2b2, c3d4, workflow_end. a1a1, b2b2, c3d4 are each 4-character strings using only [0-9a-f] characters. workflow_start/workflow_end are the reserved fixed endpoint names (explicitly exempted per AGENTS.md rule 9: 'the import schema rejects any task key that is not workflow_start, workflow_end, or a valid hex ID').

expectations.text: Adapter app/locationType from apps.json not tasks.json
expectations.evidence: task b2b2: app="Servicenow", locationType="Servicenow". Verified directly against this repo's platform/apps.json which lists {"id":"@itentialopensource/adapter-servicenow","type":"Adapter","name":"Servicenow"}, while platform/tasks.json's createChangeRequest entry reports app="ServiceNow" (capital N) — the output correctly used the apps.json value, not the tasks.json value, matching the exact trap AGENTS.md rule 3/23 warns about.

expectations.text: merge has at least 2 items in data_to_merge
expectations.evidence: a1a1.variables.incoming.data_to_merge is an array of 2 items (deviceName, vlanId), satisfying the '>=2, else silently returns null' gotcha cited in the transcript and consistent with the real asset example (which used 5 items).
